basis: Original lesson block 7 and only the corresponding D167 independent source-baseline entry.

affectedBlock.expectedMeaning: In the source's concentric spherical radial-projection model, corresponding arcs ab on the tip and AB on the screen subtend the same central angle alpha. Their arc-length ratio is the ratio R/r of the screen radius to the tip-curvature radius.
arcAngleApplicability: AB and ab denote arc lengths, not arbitrary straight chords.
The formulas AB=R alpha and ab=r alpha require the numerical angle alpha to be measured in radians.
Radian measure is the corresponding arc length divided by its circle radius, using the same length unit for both.
A numerical degree measure cannot be inserted directly into these formulas; the degree-to-radian conversion would be required.
Both arcs have the same central angle, so the common nonzero angle cancels from the arc-length ratio.
The result K=AB/ab=R/r=2 x 10^6 remains the source's geometric magnification estimate, not a universal guarantee about real instruments.
affectedBlock.protectedResult: Two million; unchanged ratio and source attribution.
affectedBlock.zhExpectation: Plain Chinese must name radians, immediately explain the arc-length/radius meaning, distinguish it from degrees, and preserve the common-angle arc proof.
affectedBlock.enExpectation: English must independently state radians, arc length divided by radius, and the same common-angle proof without relying on Chinese or a diagram.
